<description>
privacy networks set `addrMe` ("IP address peer thinks I am") in the VERSION message [as all zeroes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/f103de70de0662a1395dca2e536cf5872d86eaa2/src/net_processing.cpp#L1667).
this PR ensures we ignore it when processing VERSION message.

this fixes a fingerprint which makes it possible to correlate clearnet and privacy network IPs but it requires some not so easy preconditions:
1. we need to choose this adversarial tor/i2p peer to make an outbound connection to from our addrman
2. we need to be using a unique enough port. this would become easier in a future if we ever support random ports.

h/t to Loupe and instagibbs for finding this fingerprint!
</description>

<commits>
533fee6b9d net: ignore privacy-network peers' view of our address

- if i make an outbound connection to a tor/i2p peer
	me ---------> tor peer
  in the VERSION message the tor peer sends us back,
  there's a field which tells us about the address
  the peer thinks we are (addrMe) that can be used for
  self advertisement. Peers in privacy networks can't
  know this. So they send [::]:0.

  if a peer sends us a routable ipv4 address instead
  of [::]:0 - make sure to ignore it.

  if we don't ignore it, we can end up sending them
  as self advertisement the routable ipv4 address
  they sent us and our listening port. ignoring it
  will help prevent our custom clearnet port leaks
  to privacy networks.

9cfd601400 test: check privacy-network peers' view of our address is not used
</commits>

diff --git a/src/net.cpp b/src/net.cpp
index f31604f6c5..f72db9191c 100644
--- a/src/net.cpp
+++ b/src/net.cpp
@@ -236,7 +236,9 @@ static int GetnScore(const CService& addr)
 [[nodiscard]] static bool IsPeerAddrLocalGood(CNode *pnode)
 {
     CService addrLocal = pnode->GetAddrLocal();
-    return fDiscover && pnode->addr.IsRoutable() && addrLocal.IsRoutable() &&
+    // Tor/I2P peers can't see our clearnet address and the Tor/I2P address won't fit in addrMe (addrv1). so ignore it.
+    return fDiscover && !pnode->IsConnectedThroughPrivacyNet() &&
+           pnode->addr.IsRoutable() && addrLocal.IsRoutable() &&
            g_reachable_nets.Contains(addrLocal);
 }
 
diff --git a/src/test/net_tests.cpp b/src/test/net_tests.cpp
index 8da7f6d025..5c1c7fda92 100644
--- a/src/test/net_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/net_tests.cpp
@@ -654,6 +654,8 @@ BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(get_local_addr_for_peer_port)
     //    he sees us as.
     // 2.1. For inbound connections we must override both the address and the port.
     // 2.2. For outbound connections we must override only the address.
+    // 3. A peer on a privacy network cannot see our address, so its view of us must not
+    //    be used, neither for inbound nor for outbound connections.
 
     // Pretend that we bound to this port.
     const uint16_t bind_port = 20001;
@@ -707,6 +709,40 @@ BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(get_local_addr_for_peer_port)
     BOOST_REQUIRE(chosen_local_addr);
     BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(*chosen_local_addr, peer_us);
 
+    // An inbound privacy network peer claims to see us at a routable IPv4 address. Nothing is advertised.
+    CNetAddr i2p_addr;
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(i2p_addr.SetSpecial("udhdrtrcetjm5sxzskjyr5ztpeszydbh4dpl3pl4utgqqw2v4jna.b32.i2p"));
+    CNode peer_in_i2p{/*id=*/0,
+                      /*sock=*/nullptr,
+                      /*addrIn=*/CAddress{CService{i2p_addr, I2P_SAM31_PORT}, NODE_NETWORK},
+                      /*nKeyedNetGroupIn=*/0,
+                      /*nLocalHostNonceIn=*/0,
+                      /*addrBindIn=*/CService{},
+                      /*addrNameIn=*/std::string{},
+                      /*conn_type_in=*/ConnectionType::INBOUND,
+                      /*inbound_onion=*/false,
+                      /*network_key=*/2};
+    peer_in_i2p.fSuccessfullyConnected = true;
+    peer_in_i2p.SetAddrLocal(peer_us);
+    BOOST_CHECK(!GetLocalAddrForPeer(peer_in_i2p));
+
+    // Same for an outbound privacy network peer
+    CNetAddr onion_addr;
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(onion_addr.SetSpecial("pg6mmjiyjmcrsslvykfwnntlaru7p5svn6y2ymmju6nubxndf4pscryd.onion"));
+    CNode peer_out_onion{/*id=*/0,
+                         /*sock=*/nullptr,
+                         /*addrIn=*/CAddress{CService{onion_addr, 8333}, NODE_NETWORK},
+                         /*nKeyedNetGroupIn=*/0,
+                         /*nLocalHostNonceIn=*/0,
+                         /*addrBindIn=*/CService{},
+                         /*addrNameIn=*/std::string{},
+                         /*conn_type_in=*/ConnectionType::OUTBOUND_FULL_RELAY,
+                         /*inbound_onion=*/false,
+                         /*network_key=*/3};
+    peer_out_onion.fSuccessfullyConnected = true;
+    peer_out_onion.SetAddrLocal(peer_us);
+    BOOST_CHECK(!GetLocalAddrForPeer(peer_out_onion));
+
     m_node.args->ForceSetArg("-bind", "");
 }

{
 "summary": "Ignores the peer's observed local address (addrMe in version messages) when connected through a privacy network like Tor or I2P. The check is enforced in IsPeerAddrLocalGood so addresses reported by privacy network peers are never treated as valid local addresses for self-advertisement.",
 "problem": "Tor and I2P peers cannot see a connecting node's real IP address, yet an adversarial privacy peer can provide an arbitrary routable IP in addrMe. If accepted, the node may self-advertise that IP combined with its own listening port, creating a fingerprint that correlates clearnet and privacy network identities for nodes using non-default ports.",
 "card": "Bitcoin Core ignores the addrMe address field received from Tor and I2P peers during local address discovery. Adversarial privacy network peers cannot legitimately see a node's clearnet IP, but could feed it a routable IP that the node might self-advertise alongside its listening port. This leaks custom listening ports to privacy peers and allows correlating clearnet and privacy network identities. The vulnerability was reported by researchers and requires outbound connection to the adversary and non-default port usage.",
